Chapter I — The Realm

A flat-disc world. Walled in ice.

One vast continent floats inside the colossal Ice Wall — the frozen rim of a dying world. No loading screens. No instances. One persistent realm, shared by every commander alive.

1Persistent World
∞Routes To Drive
100+City Levels
Chapter II — The Core Hook

Cities aren't built.
They move.

Every city in the world sits on tracks, wheels, and treads, driven by coal-fed engines. You don't claim a tile and stay there. You plot a course. You drive your fortress across plains, scrap fields, and toxic shallows. The map is yours to roam.

Chapter III — Edit Mode

Design every deck. Every gun. Every banner.

In Edit Mode you place modular walls, towers, foundries and decorations using holographic blueprints. Snap, rotate, paint. No two cities will ever look the same — because none of them are templated.

Chapter IV — The Foundry

Forge engines of war.

Iron-Jaw siege tanks. Slipstream interceptors. Out-Ripper predators. From your Foundry pour molten bronze into chassis molds and field war machines no rival will see coming. Your engineering is your edge.

Chapter V — The War

Real war. Real territory. No arenas.

Two megalopolis cities collide. Treads grind. Turrets range. Marines board. Combat happens anywhere in the world — no instanced battlegrounds, no fair-fight matchmaking. The land you take is yours to hold.

Chapter VI — Syndicates

Rally as one. Move as a wall.

Link with allied commanders to form a Syndicate Rally — physical city formations that guard land-bridges, stack firepower, and share harvest. Alliances aren't a chat tab. They're a battle line.

Chapter VII — The Bazaar

A player-run economy.

Every resource is physical. Every price is set by hands at the table. Run caravans, broker harvest, corner the bronze market. The Bazaar is built by commanders, for commanders — no NPC vendors, no AI economy.

Chapter IX — Commander's Questions

20 things every commander asks.

Tap any question to expand the answer. Scroll for more.

01 What is Immortal Empires? +
A steampunk 4X MMO where entire cities are mobile war-machines on tracks and wheels. You don't just build an empire — you drive it across a living world.
02 What kind of game is this — strategy or MMO? +
Both. It blends 4X strategy (eXplore, eXpand, eXploit, eXterminate) with persistent MMO scale. Tens of thousands of commanders share one world.
03 Is the game free to play? +
Yes. Free to download, free to start, free to compete. Cosmetics, treads skins, banners, and decorations are optional. No pay-to-win.
04 When can I play it? +
Closed beta access is rolling out to early registrants first. Public launch follows. Join the waitlist to lock in beta priority.
05 What platforms will it be on? +
PC at launch. Mobile companion app for empire management, fleet coordination, and chat. Console is on the long-term roadmap.
06 How do moving cities actually work? +
Every city sits on tracks, wheels, or treads, powered by coal-fed engines. You plot routes across the world map. Your city physically moves — and so do your enemies'.
07 Can my city be attacked while I'm offline? +
Cities have shields, defensive turrets, and Syndicate protection. Offline raids exist but are expensive to mount. Smart routing and alliances keep you safe while you sleep.
08 How big is the world? +
One persistent flat-disc world bounded by the Ice Wall. Thousands of square kilometers of explorable terrain — plains, oil flats, toxic shallows, scrap deserts, and the central megalopolis ring.
09 How many players are in one world? +
Massive scale. Tens of thousands per realm. Realms shard during peak war seasons but the persistent map remains shared.
10 Can I play solo? +
Yes. Solo commanders can level a city to L100, harvest, trade, and run contracts. But the biggest rewards — Realm Bosses, megalopolis sieges, land-bridge control — require Syndicates.
11 Is there PvE content too? +
Plenty. Realm Bosses (massive AI megalopolis cities), Harvest fields, scrap runs, escort contracts, and lore quests through the University Web.
12 How does combat work? +
Real-time territorial battles between moving cities. Position your treads, range your turrets, target enemy engines, board with marines. Commanders give orders; the city executes.
13 What does my character actually do? +
You're the Commander. You customize your appearance, walk your decks, command from the Bridge, negotiate with rivals, and lead your crew. Your city is your second body.
14 How does progression work? +
Cities level from 1 (small fortress) to 100+ (megalopolis). Unlock structures via the University Web — a sprawling skill grid with branching paths in War, Industry, Diplomacy, and Engineering.
15 Can I customize my city's look? +
Edit Mode lets you place modular walls, towers, decks, and decorations using holographic blueprints. Banners, paint schemes, and tread skins are all yours to design.
16 What are Syndicates? +
Player alliances. Up to dozens of cities can link in formation — Syndicate Rally — guarding chokepoints, sharing harvest, and stacking firepower against rivals.
17 How does the economy work? +
Resources are physical. You mine them, haul them, and trade them in the Bazaar or with other commanders directly. Markets are player-driven — no NPC vendors setting prices.
18 Can I lose my city permanently? +
Cities can be captured, not deleted. A captured commander goes to the Brig and can be ransomed or rescued. You keep your blueprints; you rebuild stronger.
19 Is there cosmetic gear and customization? +
Yes — themed steampunk apparel, accessories, hats, goggles, signature outfits, and weapon skins. The Loyalty Store rotates limited-edition cosmetics every season.
20 Will my beta progress carry over? +
Beta accounts keep their character identity, name, founding banner, and an exclusive Founders' Tread Skin. City progress resets at launch — the war begins fresh.
